extracted.intended_audience: prospective improv students and performers seeking training at The Annoyance Theatre (Chicago)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, curricula, and policies for The Annoyance Theatre's improv training program (AP1-AP5, CRASS, musicals, intensives, workshops), including learning objectives, prerequisites, attendance/makeup rules, and community policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on individual point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance philosophy focuses on the individual; giving students feedback and support to allow them to find and enhance their personal point of view and creative voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes are designed to help each student identify who they are as an improviser and to strengthen their comedic voice; instructors provide individual feedback and set performance goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take Care Of Yourself First
rubrics_metrics.description: "Take Care Of Yourself First" is a core concept drilled in AP2 and emphasized throughout the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn personal responsibility in a scene, making clear choices, and ensuring they are initiating and maintaining their own contributions before relying on partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive initiations and strong point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Annoyance philosophy emphasizes decisive scene initiations and having a strong point of view on stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training addresses how first seconds of scenes affect the rest of the scene and encourages initiations that clearly establish 'your deal' and worldview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding or creating the game
rubrics_metrics.description: Students learn to find or create the 'game' of a scene as a central improv skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coursework covers recognizing patterns/games and using them to drive scenes (applies across short-form and long-form work).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Yes, and" and when to say "no"
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction on how to say 'yes, and' and also when to appropriately say 'no' in improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on balancing agreement with scene needs and making choices that serve the scene's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object and environment work
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of object and environment work as inspiration for character and scene choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students practice embodying objects and building rich, varied environments to expand scenes and character physicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating and sustaining character
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning and continued development of character work across levels (AP2–AP5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on embodying character, embellishing the world, and maintaining voice in multiple-person or split scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic improv (physical and emotional choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing scenes organically based on physical and emotional choices rather than forcing plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn to develop scenes through honest physical/emotional commitments that naturally escalate or change the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stretching performer and pushing specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: AP4 focuses on stretching performers and pushing unique specificity in choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work includes exercises to expand risk-taking, specificity of detail, and distinctiveness of comedic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping voice in group scenes and split-scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining an individual voice when working in larger scenes or split scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes strategies to preserve individuality while collaborating and supporting ensemble coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making rich, varied environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for creating layered, believable, and varied scene environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises and feedback focus on environmental specificity to support character interactions and scene stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensemble building and collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: AP5 emphasizes ensemble work, collaboration, show pacing, rehearsal process, and good rehearsal habits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP5 classes culminate in runs of shows and provide instructor feedback for both ensemble and individual improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show creation and run-of-shows experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Students create original improv shows (AP5/CRASS/MI3) and perform in actual audience runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP5 features a four-week run alongside the last classes; CRASS converts improv into written sketch revues or plays; MI3 features runs and instructor feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP1 curriculum: introductory breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: AP1 introduces Chicago-style improv and covers rules of improv, group mind, 'yes, and', finding the game, long-form, short-form, writing via improv, direction, object/environment work, and show introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This course is for new improv/acting/comedy students; culminates in an optional student showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP2 curriculum: beginnings and 'your deal'
rubrics_metrics.description: AP2 focuses on the first seconds of scenes, 'Your Deal', beginning character development, trusting instincts, and responsibility to operate without censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite: AP1 or equivalent experience; includes individual feedback on tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP3 curriculum: scenic development and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: AP3 covers scene work: acknowledging realities of partners, finding 'highways and bi-ways' to extend scenes, managing context, creating surprising choices, multiple patterns/games, three-person/group work, repairing scenes, DaDa scenes, and justification as a tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite: AP2; includes personal challenge goals and culminates in optional showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP4 curriculum: fine-tuning and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: AP4 focuses on tightening performance via stretching the performer, pushing unique specificity, maintaining voice in multi-person scenes, making rich environments, embodiment, and organic improv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite: AP3; includes individual feedback and culminates in optional showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRASS: turning improv into written works
rubrics_metrics.description: CRASS classes use improv to create written sketch revues or one-act plays; students may take on roles beyond actor/writer and are expected to rehearse outside class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRASS is more intensive than AP1-5 and requires additional out-of-class work; CRASS1 focuses on sketch revues, CRASS2 adds narrative play complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Improv prerequisites and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical Improv (MI1–MI3) requires completion of AP3; MI1 introduces improvising songs, MI2 covers a cohesive half-hour improvised musical, MI3 focuses on narrative form and includes show runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students do not have to be good singers to succeed; MISG covers styles/genres to expand range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive structure and prerequisites (Summer Intensive Part 1 & 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Intensive Part 1 is an overview; Part 2 covers advanced techniques and requires completion of Part 1; the full AP program is normally 20 hours over eight weeks, intensives compress content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 1 completion required for Part 2; intensives may cram 20 hours into 6, so Part 2 assumes shared baseline experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class meeting frequency and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Most classes meet once a week on the same day each week; typical times listed (M-Thu 6:30-9pm, Sat/Sun 1-3:30pm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be sure of their schedules before registering due to attendance and refund policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional student showcase requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Many classes culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showcase participation is optional but presented as culmination of course work and learning outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites and skipping AP1 policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No prerequisite for AP1; students may skip AP1 and start at AP2 only if they have completed a full year at iO, The Second City, The Pit, The Magnet or UCB training programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming equivalent experience, students should note prior schools in comments so staff may confirm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression prerequisites (AP2→AP3→AP4→AP5)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP3 requires completion of AP2; AP4 requires completion of AP3; AP5 requires completion of AP4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must meet these prerequisites before signing up for higher levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance limit to progress
rubrics_metrics.description: To progress to the next level, students may miss no more than 2 sessions of their class day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must miss a class for AP1-AP4 there is an opportunity to make up that class on another day that week, provided other classes meet; make-up spots are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up class policy and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Make-up classes are available only for AP1-AP4 (not AP5, AP6-1, AP6-2, or electives); only two make-up spots are available per class and you must sign up to attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make-up is subject to availability and only applies to the current term's class; sign-up links provided per level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration payment and refund policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration payments are non-refundable, non-transferable, and can be applied only to the current term’s class for which you signed up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies regardless of being cast in a show, getting a new job, or other schedule changes; enrollment holds a space that cannot be given to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship program criteria and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity and Inclusion Scholarship funds full tuition for 2 awardees for AP1-5 and CRASS1-2; applications are accepted during specified windows and awards allow registration within 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees may register for the announced session (based on availability) or any time within 6 months following award date; no more than 2 sessions may be skipped at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment reporting and investigation process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance partners with WorkShield for reporting harassment or discrimination; reports may be anonymous or named, and will be investigated with intent to hear both sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If anonymous, follow-up may be more difficult; contact via atb.workshieldportal.com or hotline 846.946.5558.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance states DEI and accessibility are central; the space is intended to be safe for people regardless of race, age, gender identity, disability, economic status, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility is fully accessible (elevator, ramps); multiple single-occupancy restrooms available; use whichever bathroom matches gender identity or expression; staff invite suggestions to better meet needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: All teachers are ensemble members who have learned and performed with The Annoyance and have first-hand experience with the Annoyance approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors provide individualized feedback and are positioned to teach the Annoyance-specific philosophy and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload expectations for intensive/CRASS classes
rubrics_metrics.description: CRASS and intensives require additional rehearsal and work outside class hours; CRASS students may have responsibilities beyond acting/writing (costumes, props, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classes are more intensive than standard AP levels and expect greater outside commitment from students.
